verdict.rationale: Apple documents that M4 Pro supports up to 64GB of unified memory and 273GB/s of memory bandwidth, and claims LLMs run smoothly on device, with MLX as a first-party framework for generative models. Nothing in the evidence shows a 70B-class quantized model actually running on M4 Pro or measures its speed, so practicality at that size is unproven. Missing for 10: explicit 70B-class model support or sizing guidance, hands-on or independent tokens-per-second benchmarks, and corroboration that 64GB is enough headroom for 70B quantized inference in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a large local LLM (70B-class, quantized) on this platform — enough addressable memory and published memory bandwidth to make local inference practical

citations.quote: M4 Pro supports up to 64GB of fast unified memory and 273GB/s of memory bandwidth
large language models (LLMs) and other large projects run smoothly and on device
MLX is an open-source array framework that lets you experiment with, training, researching, and fine-tuning generative models on Apple Silicon.
